extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, petitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners/OPLA staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for filing, preliminarily handling, and adjudicating petitions alleging public use or on-sale bars (37 CFR 1.292) and for submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials under MPEP §724. Covers timing, content, service, examiner prima facie determinations, hearings, testimony, final decisions, and confidential-material handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of petition under 37 CFR 1.292
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be "submitted prior to the date the application was published or the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, whichever occurs first."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit as soon as possible after becoming aware of the application; early submission (ideally before the Office acts on the application) maximizes consideration. Petitions filed after publication or notice of allowance will be dismissed as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal content and filing requirements for 37 CFR 1.292 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition is reviewed to see whether it contains affidavits or declarations and exhibits to establish the facts alleged, whether the papers have been filed in duplicate (or one copy served on applicant), and whether the required fee has been tendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure affidavits/declarations and supporting exhibits are included; file duplicate copies or serve a copy on applicant; include required petition fee. OPLA staff will ascertain fulfillment of these formal requirements before forwarding to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and Certificate of Service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effort should be made to effect service of the petition upon the attorney or agent of record or upon the applicant; the petition filed in the Office should reflect, by an appropriate "Certificate of Service," that service has been made as provided in 37 CFR 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve a complete copy (including photographs, drawings, exhibits, flowcharts, etc.). If service is not possible, file duplicate so the Office can attempt service. If petition does not indicate service and no duplicate filed, the Office may contact applicant to determine service and may request a duplicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling and handling of "REISSUE LITIGATION" petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside envelope and the top right-hand portion of the petition should be marked with the words "REISSUE LITIGATION." The notations preferably should be written in a bright color with a felt point marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail such petitions to "Mail Stop Petition" or hand-carry to the USPTO Customer Window to ensure prompt receipt. Hand-carried petitions and replies may only be delivered to the Customer Window (address provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue-application petition timing and extension rules (37 CFR 1.176/1.182/1.183)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition with regard to a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the filing of the reissue application in the Official Gazette. Requests for extension of the 2-month period must be filed as a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and accompanied by the petition fee in 37 CFR 1.17(f); petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 with fee 1.17(f) may waive the 2-month delay in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a later-filed petition is submitted, petitioner must explain why additional time is necessary and describe the allegations. Such requests will be critically reviewed and granted only for demonstrated need; do not assume the full 2-month delay is automatically available.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA preliminary handling and file retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under 37 CFR 1.292 should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA). A member of OPLA staff will ascertain whether the formal requirements have been fulfilled and will order the application file and determine its status so appropriate action may be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petitioner cannot identify the pending application by application number, OPLA will forward papers to the appropriate TC Director for an identification search. OPLA may accept or refuse additional papers at its discretion; protracted filing is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie showing standard for public use/on-sale (examiner determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case is established by the petition if the examiner finds that the facts asserted in the affidavit(s) or declaration(s), as supported by the exhibits, if later proved true by testimony taken in the public use proceeding, would result in a statutory bar to the claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make this determination the examiner must identify exactly what was in public use or on sale, whether it was in use or on sale in this country more than 1 year before the effective filing date, and whether the pending claims "read" on or are obvious over what has been shown. The examiner should compare all pending claims with the alleged public use/on-sale matter, not just those identified by petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when petition alleges obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where the petition alleges only that the claims are obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the petition should include prior art or other information on which it relies and explain how the prior art or other information in combination with the subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale renders the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not expected to perform a prior art search in evaluating the petition. However, if the examiner is aware of prior art or other information which in the examiner's opinion renders the claims obvious in view of the alleged public use/on-sale matter, the examiner may determine that a prima facie case of obviousness is made out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner memorandum to OPLA content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: After making the determination, the examiner will forward a memorandum to the OPLA staff member stating findings and decision as to whether a prima facie case has been established. The findings should include a summary of the alleged facts, a comparison of at least one claim with the device alleged to be in public use or on sale, and any other pertinent facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should be prepared in triplicate and addressed to the OPLA staff member; include enough detail to aid OPLA in conducting the preliminary hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hearing constraints and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner concludes that a prima facie case has been established, the Director may hold a preliminary hearing; parties will be notified of the time and date. No new evidence is to be introduced or discussed at this hearing. The format of the hearing is established by the OPLA staff member and the examiner may attend only as an observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte situations, avoid discussing matters of the application file not already known to the petitioner. The hearing notice functions as an order to show cause why a public use proceeding should not be held. After the hearing OPLA decides whether to institute public use proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony requirement for establishing statutory bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory bar can only be established by testimony taken in accordance with normal rules of evidence, including the right of cross-examination. The affidavits or declarations and exhibits presented with the petition are not to be considered part of the testimony and in no case can they be used as evidence on behalf of the party submitting them unless they are submitted as part of the petitioner's testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.157(a) limits noncompelled direct testimony to affidavits. Do not treat petition affidavits/declarations as conclusive evidence—live testimony and cross-examination are required to establish the bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling rules for testimony, records, and briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will set a schedule for testimony and for filing the record and briefs (sample schedule items A–F for petitioner testimony, applicant objections, supplemental evidence, cross-examination requests, cross-examination, rebuttal testimony). One copy of each party's record and exhibits is due (date specified). Petitioner’s and applicant’s briefs have specified due dates; applicant and petitioner may agree on a different schedule provided the last brief is due no later than the date set forth and a copy of the new schedule is filed. No extension of time will be permitted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Any petition to extend the time for filing the last brief must be filed under 37 CFR 1.136(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified transcript of a deposition must be filed in the USPTO within one month after the date of deposition (37 CFR 41.157). All papers in the public use proceeding shall be served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248. Examiner should indicate specific dates to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of testimony in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In all public use proceedings, whether the ultimate issue is anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) or obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103, testimony will be limited to the issues of public use or on sale. No testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep testimony focused strictly on whether the alleged activity occurred and the facts establishing public use or on-sale activity; arguments about obviousness should be handled by other evidentiary means, not live testimony in these proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision standard and required written action
rubrics_metrics.description: The final decision of the examiner should be analogous to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences' analysis in an interference proceeding, analyzing the testimony and stating conclusions. The examiner is not bound by the prior prima facie finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes a public use or sale bar exists, enter a rejection predicated on the evidence and findings. Even if no rejection is made, the written action should reflect that the evidence of 35 U.S.C. 102(b) activity was considered. If no prima facie case or it was rebutted, the written action should so indicate. Use of reasons for allowance under 37 CFR 1.104(e) may be appropriate. Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 to vacate the examiner's decision are entertained only for clear error; appellate review under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 141–145 may follow after return to ex parte status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose trade secret/proprietary/protective-order information (37 CFR 1.56/1.555)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors and others covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c) and 1.555 have a duty to disclose to the Office information they are aware of which is material to patentability. 37 CFR 1.56(b) states that information is material when it is not cumulative and (1) it establishes, by itself or in combination with other information, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes, or is inconsistent with, a position the applicant takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty applies regardless of whether the information is a trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order. A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of the evidence standard, giving each claim term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials (MPEP §724.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material considered trade secret or proprietary, and any material subject to a protective order, must be clearly labeled as such and be filed in a sealed, clearly labeled, envelope or container. Each document or item must be clearly labeled as a "Trade Secret" document or item, a "Proprietary" document or item, or as an item or document "Subject To Protective Order." Avoid using the terms "Confidential," "Restricted" or "Restricted Data." If "Subject to Protective Order," the proceeding and tribunal must be set forth on each document. The envelope or container must be accompanied by a transmittal letter containing the same identifying information and stating the materials are submitted under MPEP §724. A petition under 37 CFR 1.59 with fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) to expunge should accompany the envelope if expungement is sought if the materials are found not material to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete identifying information (application no., filed date, title, TC art unit, examiner). Labels may include "DO NOT SCAN" and specific template fields. Hand-carrying to the Customer Service Window is recommended to avoid mishandling; mailing address to the Commissioner for Patents is an alternative. Office will date-stamp and note receipt and place materials in artifact folder (IFW) or retain envelope for paper files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and required labeling for sealed envelopes
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate label examples include: (A) "TRADE SECRET MATERIAL NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC. TO BE OPENED ONLY BY EXAMINER OR OTHER AUTHORIZED U.S. PATENT AND TRADEMARK OFFICE EMPLOYEE. DO NOT SCAN" with application-identifying fields; (B) similar text for "PROPRIETARY MATERIAL"; (C) similar text for "MATERIAL SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER" with tribunal identification and status fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided templates and include all identifying information (application no., title, TC art unit, examiner). The envelope/container's transmittal letter must repeat the identifying info and the claim that materials are trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order under MPEP §724.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of materials appropriate for MPEP §724.02 submission (and exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials contemplated for submission under MPEP §724.02 include information "material to patentability" but do not include information favorable to patentability (e.g., evidence of commercial success). Such favorable information should not be submitted under MPEP §724.02. If trade secret/proprietary materials are submitted in amendments, arguments, or affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.132, they will be made of record and will not be given any special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protestors may submit materials under MPEP §724.02 before publication if they have access; after publication no protest may be filed without applicant consent. Parties served cannot be guaranteed to keep materials secret; comments on submitted materials should either avoid disclosing details or be submitted in a separate sealed paper under MPEP §724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office treatment and handling of submitted trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials (MPEP §724.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods differ depending on whether the materials are submitted in an original application covered by 35 U.S.C. 122 or in a reissue or reexamination file open to the public. Upon receipt, the transmittal letter and envelope/container are date-stamped, brought to the examiner's attention, noted in the file "Contents," and the file face will have a notation indicating such materials have been filed (e.g., "TRADE SECRET MATERIALS FILED WHICH ARE NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW processing the envelope is placed in an Artifact folder; for paper files the confidential information is retained in the envelope. The location of the material is specified and similar notations are made for proprietary or protective order materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release, expungement, and public availability rules for submitted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application file and contents become available to the public pursuant to 37 CFR 1.11 or 1.14, materials submitted under MPEP §724.02 will only be released to the public with any other application papers if no petition to expunge (37 CFR 1.59) was filed prior to mailing of a notice of allowability or abandonment, or if a petition to expunge was filed and denied. Prior to mailing notice of allowability or abandonment, the examiner reviews the file to determine if a petition to expunge is present. If the application is being allowed and the materials are found not to be material, the petition to expunge will be granted and the materials expunged. If found material, the petition will be denied and the materials will become part of the record and available to the public upon issuance. With mailing of notice of abandonment, if a petition to expunge has been filed, irrespective of materiality the petition to expunge will be granted and the materials expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials maintained in the original sealed envelope are not publicly available until materiality determination. If no petition to expunge is filed and the application is abandoned, the materials may become public under 37 CFR 1.14. Existence and outcome of petitions control eventual public availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific handling for applications covered by 35 U.S.C. 122
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP §724.02 in an application covered by 35 U.S.C. 122 will be maintained in the original envelope or container (clearly marked "Not Open To The Public") and will not be publicly available until a determination has been made as to whether the information is material to patentability. After publication, release will be governed by petition-to-expunge rules described above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is to be abandoned and a petition to expunge has been filed, the materials will be expunged prior to mailing notice of abandonment irrespective of materiality; if application is being allowed, the examiner will determine whether any portion or all of the information is material prior to mailing notice of allowability.
